chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about the pigeons of the Sanctuary being hunted in the open country, so he said: 'The pigeons of the Sanctuary are not to be hunted wherever they are, if it is known that they are from the pigeons of the Sanctuary.' And whoever plucks a feather from a pigeon of the Sanctuary, let him give charity with that hand.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on hunting pigeons of the Haram while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that the sanctity of the Haram's pigeons is intrinsic and not limited to the sacred precincts, extending their protection to the open country (Hill) where they are known to belong. This ruling underscores the concept of *Hurmah* (sanctity) attached to specific creatures of the Sanctuary, requiring expiation (*Kaffarah*) even for minor acts like plucking a single feather, reflecting the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between intentional and accidental transgressions during Hajj.
